claims.text: The ride deviated. The platform's own optimal route for this booking was 14.0 km (EV-TRIP-00107, optimal_route_source 'routing-engine-v3.2'), while the driver's GPS polyline covers 17.57 km (EV-GPS-00107, derived.deviation.trace_distance_km) - an excess of 3.57 km, or 25.5% of optimal. Both POL-RD-01 gates pass: the excess is greater than 0.8 km and greater than 20% of optimal, so the deviation is ESTABLISHED, and it is established on the trace figure, which governs over the rounded trip_record copy. I disclose that EV-GPS-00107 is IMPAIRED at weight 0.30 on the pre-pass, with issue codes GPS_DRIFT and IMPLAUSIBLE_SPEED, and I do not present it as clean evidence.

The GPS impairment does not reach policy level. Under POL-RD-07 a trace is impaired for policy purposes only on a gap over 90 seconds, a straight-line jump over 500 m, or a sustained sampling interval over 30 seconds. This trace has no gaps at all (gaps empty, max_gap_sec 0.0), samples every 10 seconds, and its worst outlier jump is 331.8 m - under the 500 m limb. The deviation may therefore be established on the trace, and the pre-pass down-weighting of EV-GPS-00107 operates under POL-GEN-02 alone, which is a different question.

Corroboration independent of the trace exists, as POL-RD-08 requires here because rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 5 against deviation_claims_60d_substantiated of 1, and the excess is under 30%. In EV-CHAT-00107 the rider challenges the Whitley exit - 'why exit at whitley? CTE goes straight down what' - and the driver does not dispute it, replying only 'cte very jam tonight boss', which concedes that he left the CTE. On top of that the driver's counterparty statement on file admits the route outright: 'I went by Newton and Kim Seng to avoid it.' Both are independent of the GPS trace and both fall within the POL-RD-07(ii) list of corroborating sources.

No closure or advisory exoneration is available. The only traffic advisory in the bundle, EV-ADVIS-00107-01, is MISSING at weight 0.0: no congestion advisory was issued for the CTE on the evening of 18 July 2026, and the driver's assertion that CTE was jammed names no artifact. POL-RD-03 requires an advisory that names a road or segment the optimal route traverses and carries a validity window overlapping the pass; there is none, so no excess is exonerated and no closure-adjusted optimal route may be constructed.

The burden has shifted to the driver and he has not discharged it. POL-RD-08 requires the driver, once the rider has shown the excess, to point to a specific artifact and a specific clause to excuse it, and it states expressly that a general assertion that traffic was bad, unsupported by a traffic_advisory ID, does not discharge that burden. The driver's chat reply and his counterparty statement both assert a jam, but cite no advisory, and the advisory artifact EV-ADVIS-00107-01 is missing from the record. The 3.57 km excess therefore stands unexplained.

This was not a rider-requested detour. EV-CHAT-00107 holds only two messages, both sent well into the trip: the rider asking why the driver left the CTE, and the driver answering that it was jammed. There is no rider instruction to go via Newton, Newton Circus or Kim Seng Road, waypoint_hint is null on both messages, and no road is named by the rider. POL-RD-04 is unavailable on this record and excuses no part of the excess.

The refund is arithmetic, not discretionary. This trip is METERED, so POL-RD-02 runs against the booked 14.0 km / 24.0 min optimal: recomputed_fare = ((3.80 + 0.75 x 14.0 + 0.28 x 24.0) x 1.35) + 0.80 platform fee = (21.02 x 1.35) + 0.80 = 29.177. Refund = 36.60 charged_total - 29.177 = 7.423, rounded UP to SGD 7.45. The 1.35 multiplier is read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier on EV-FARE-00107, which is the only artifact that carries it - the trip_record has no such field, and reading surge as absent would double the figure. The refund is above the 0.50 de minimis and far below 90% of charged_total, so the outcome is a PARTIAL_REFUND of 7.45.

POL-RD-11 does not close the distance-refund route on this trip. fare_breakdown.fare_model on EV-FARE-00107 is METERED and quoted_fare_sgd is null; the rider was billed per kilometre (17.6 km at 0.75) and per minute (34.0 min at 0.28) on a metered card, so the distance and time charges were not fixed at booking and a POL-RD-02 recomputation is the correct remedy.

The rider is presently carrying the entire disputed charge: fare_breakdown.payment_status on EV-FARE-00107 is CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd is 0.00, so the 36.60 has been collected and nothing returned. A PARTIAL_REFUND of 7.45 leaves the rider not carrying the deviated portion of the fare, which is what a rider win means for a rider-filed dispute under POL-GEN-03.

I do not press the POL-RD-06 uplift, because the record does not support it. The excess of 25.5% is below the 50% materiality limb and the 3.57 km excess is below the 8.0 km limb, so this deviation is not MATERIAL; and in any event driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 1 against completed_trips_90d of 619 - below both the count of 3 and the 0.05 ratio the clause requires. No repeat pattern is established, so I claim no FULL_REFUND uplift and no conduct referral on this record.

Escalation is not mandated on this record. The deciding facts are not carried by the 0.30 trace alone: the optimal distance the excess is measured against is carried by EV-TRIP-00107 at weight 1.0, and the route actually driven is independently admitted by the driver in EV-CHAT-00107 at weight 1.0. Under POL-GEN-02(2), where two or more independent artifacts carry the deciding fact the cap is the MAXIMUM of their weights rather than the minimum, so no POL-RD-10(1) confidence-floor trigger fires; and because the trace meets none of the POL-RD-07(a) to (c) limbs, POL-RD-10(3) does not fire either.

ruling.explanation:
This case goes to a human reviewer. The $36.60 fare is held - neither refunded nor confirmed - and no compensation is paid. Here is the reasoning, for both of you.

To the rider: your central point is correct. The booked optimal route was 14.0 km (EV-TRIP-00107) and the GPS trace runs 17.57 km (EV-GPS-00107), an excess of 3.57 km, or 25.5%, so both POL-RD-01 gates (over 0.8 km and over 20%) pass and the deviation is ESTABLISHED on the trace figure, which governs over the rounded 17.6 km copy on the trip record. The driver's 'jam' answer does not excuse it: POL-RD-03 requires a traffic advisory naming the affected road with a validity window, and no advisory was issued that evening (EV-ADVIS-00107-01 is MISSING, weight 0.0, issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT); a general assertion that traffic was bad, naming no advisory, carries no weight under POL-RD-08. POL-RD-04 does not apply (the chat holds no rider instruction to detour - the only two messages are mid-trip), nor POL-RD-05 (no amended pickup or dropoff), nor POL-RD-11 (the fare is METERED, not an upfront quote), nor POL-RD-12 (not a pooled trip). No POL-RD-09 pass-through or billing-integrity correction arises: the fare breakdown has no ERP gantries, no tolls, no airport surcharge, no waiting fee and no promo. The deviation is not MATERIAL (25.5% is under 50%, 3.57 km under 8.0 km) and there is no repeat-deviation pattern (1 flag against 619 completed trips), so there is no POL-RD-06 full-refund uplift and no driver-conduct referral.

Why I cannot decide it here: the size of the excess rests on a single artifact, the GPS trace EV-GPS-00107, which the admissibility pre-pass has down-weighted to 0.30 and tagged with GPS_DRIFT and IMPLAUSIBLE_SPEED (a 331.8 m multipath jump on the final Raffles Place approach, implying impossible speeds). Two things must be said of it, as the policy requires. First, it is impaired at the schema level and its weight is 0.30. Second, it is NOT impaired for policy purposes under POL-RD-07 - there is no gap over 90 s, its worst jump is 331.8 m (under the 500 m limb) and it samples every 10 s - so a deviation may properly be established on it, and it is. The difficulty is POL-GEN-02(2): my confidence cannot exceed the lowest weight among the artifacts carrying the deciding fact, and here nothing independent carries it. The excess distance is the deciding fact. The trip record's 17.6 km is a rounded copy of the same measurement, which POL-RD-01 forbids citing for the threshold test; the fare's 17.6 km is the same measurement on the meter. The driver's admissions - 'cte very jam tonight boss' in the chat and 'I went by Newton and Kim Seng' in his statement - are real corroboration of the ROUTE and they satisfy the extra corroboration POL-RD-08 demands because of the rider's 60-day claim history, but neither supplies an independent MEASUREMENT of the distance. Confidence is therefore capped at 0.30, below the 0.70 platform floor, and POL-RD-10(1) makes escalation mandatory and terminal. POL-RD-10(3) does not fire, precisely because the trace is not policy-impaired. Had confidence permitted a ruling, POL-RD-02 would give: charged_total $36.60; recomputed_fare ((3.80 + 0.75 x 14.0 + 0.28 x 24.0) x 1.35) + $0.80 = $29.177; refund $7.45 (the 1.35 multiplier read from fare_breakdown.surge_multiplier, the only artifact carrying it). That figure is not payable now.

To the driver: I have not accepted your traffic explanation, which names no advisory and carries no weight under POL-RD-08, and your submission that the 0.30 weight caps confidence and compels escalation under POL-GEN-02(2) and POL-RD-10(1) is the reason this case cannot be decided here. Your other points stand: the excess is below both materiality limbs, so no POL-RD-06 uplift or referral, and there are no charge lines to correct under POL-RD-09.

What would settle it, for the reviewer: a drift-corrected or clean trace over the final approach, or any independent measurement of the distance driven - for example a rider-side track, or a distance the platform derived independently of this trace. On that evidence the $7.45 figure can be confirmed or adjusted.
